Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. West Indies are seen in a huddle near the ropes. Jos Buttler and Phil Salt are the openers for England. Akeal Hosein to start with the new ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

England had a rocky start as the batters hit some boundaries and put pressure on the bowlers. Chris Woakes read the pitch well and relied on the slower deliveries. He was rewarded with a very important wicket of Mayers. Jos Buttler came out with another master stroke and brought in the spinners. Adil Rashid got two wickets in his first two overs while Rehan Ahmed took one. They had managed to get England back in the game and transferred the pressure on the opponents. The bowlers were soon put under pressure as King and Powell started hitting boundaries. Sam Curran gave his team the next breakthrough as he sent the skipper back to the pavilion. Tymal Mills struck in the final over of the innings as he cleaned up Russell and Holder in successive deliveries. The target for England is 177 runs. Will the batters be able to chase down the target? We will find out in a while.

West Indies had a very strong start to their innings. Brandon King looked to be aggressive from the start whereas his partner, Kyle Mayers took his time and then unleashed his power. Mayers hit a few good shots but then picked the wrong shot and was dismissed. After that partnerships and boundaries were hard to come for the hosts as Nicholas Pooran, Shai Hope, and Shimron Hetmyer were sent back in quick succession while King stood on the other end watching his teammates come in and walk back to the pavilion. King and the skipper, Rovman Powell put up a strong stand and stabilized the innings. King completed his half-century which gave some momentum to the batters. Powell also was dismissed but not before he too completed his half-century. King and Russell continued their aggressive approach till the end and managed to go well over the 170-run mark.

What an incredible innings. At first, it looked like the West Indies were in control then the Englishmen bounced back until the Windies took control back in the later stages of the game. A powerful ending by the hosts as they managed to put 176 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. We will witness history in the making as Jacqueline Williams will become the first female umpire from the West Indies to stand in a men's T20I between two full members. Brandon King and Kyle Mayers will open the batting innings. Moeen Ali has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...

Pitch report - Nikhil Uttamchandani is pitchside and he says that there are some cracks in the middle, but there might be moisture under it as there was rain. The spinners might get some grip, and the batters need to be a little watchful. He feels that it will be a high scoring match and that the average first innings score on this ground is around 170.

Rovman Powell the skipper of West Indies, says that he feels it is a pretty good surface and he would have preferred to bowl first too. He adds that they will try to make full use of the powerplay. Ends by saying that Gudakesh Motie comes in for Romario Shepherd.

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England, says that they will bowl first. Adds that the Windies side has been fantastic and they will look to bounce back and look to win this one. Ends by mentioning that Moeen Ali comes in for Ben Duckett.
England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (C/WK), Will Jacks, Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Sam Curran, Moeen Ali (In for Ben Duckett), Chris Woakes, Rehan Ahmed, Adil Rashid, Tymal Mills.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Kyle Mayers, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell (C), Gudakesh Motie (In for Romario Shepherd), Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of England. They have elected to BOWL first.

England on the other hand will hope for a good comeback in this game. With 4 matches to go in the series it is not too late to shift the momentum in their favor. Phil Salt and Jos Buttler are in good form at the top of the order but the form of their middle order especially Harry Brook will be a topic of concern. They need someone to give a powerful end to their batting innings down the order. Rehan Ahmed is bowling brilliantly and taking wickets as well along with Adil Rashid. The pacers are lacking in the wickets department and they will need to take a few of them with the new ball to create pressure on the opposition. This is expected to be a nail-biting encounter between these two nations. Stay with us as the action will begin soon. Toss and team news to follow.

The hosts, West Indies have taken an early lead in the series by winning the first game but there is still a long way to go and they will have to maintain their form. Andre Russell and Alzarri Joseph were brilliant with the ball taking 3 wickets each along with some support from the others. In the batting department, their top order also looks in a top-notch rhythm. Shimron Hetmyer and Nicholas Pooran can improve their form but there won't be any pressure on them with the way Rovman Powell and Andre Russell ended the innings. They will want to keep their form consistent and build their winning streak by clinching a victory in this game as well.
Hello and a very warm welcome folks. The stage is set for the 2nd T20I between the 5-match series between West Indies and England which will be played at St George's, Grenada
